outcome: No proof, counterexample, new case, or bound improvement on the Marcus-de Oliveira determinantal conjecture was found in the window; the only post-snapshot item is a February 2025 survey paper that reviews pre-existing (largely pre-2024) partial results without adding new mathematics.
summary: The Marcus-de Oliveira determinantal conjecture (det(A+B) lies in the convex hull of n! points, for normal A, B) remains open. Searches for a proof, disproof, new special case, or bound improvement since 26 January 2024 turned up nothing new. The only item published in the window is Bebiano and da Providência, 'Revisiting the Marcus-de Oliveira Conjecture' (Mathematics, MDPI 13(5):711, published 22 February 2025), which is explicitly a survey: it 'reviews the main achievements relating to this open problem... and aims to bring attention... to stimulate the development of original approaches' — it establishes no new result, so it does not change status. The Khadejah Homadi Auburn thesis surfaced repeatedly in searches ('Progress on the Marcus-de Oliveira Determinantal Conjecture') is from 2017, well before the window, and compiles prior known partial cases (n-2 equal eigenvalues, essentially-Hermitian pairs, a class of normal dilations from a 2020/2021 paper) — none of that is new either and none postdates the frozen revision. A July 2026 arXiv preprint (2607.21163) that surfaced under similar search terms concerns a different conjecture entirely — a normal-matrix extension of a determinantal conjecture of Lin about det(A*A+|BA|^p) vs det(AA*+|A*B*|^p) — and does not touch the Marcus-de Oliveira sum-of-normal-matrices conjecture; it is excluded as out of scope (§3.1, a related/different problem, not a case of this one). The dedicated Wikipedia article 'Determinantal conjecture' is a stub with no post-2024 content. No AI system was mentioned in connection with this conjecture anywhere in the search results; general searches for LLM-solved conjectures returned unrelated problems (cycle double cover conjecture, Goldbach-related work), confirming no crossover. This is a well-evidenced 'nothing happened' case.
competing_reading: One could argue the 2025 MDPI survey itself constitutes a form of progress by consolidating scattered partial results and explicitly restating open sub-questions (e.g., the n=4, X Hermitian/Y normal subconjecture) in a way that could focus future research — but a survey with no new theorem does not change what a careful reader would write in the Wikipedia bullet, so it does not meet the bar for `progress`.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or publication dated after 26 January 2024 that proves a new case of the conjecture (e.g., resolving the n=4 Hermitian/normal subconjecture), improves on the known partial results, or exhibits/rules out a counterexample; alternatively, explicit confirmation from a specialist survey (e.g., a future edition of the MDPI-hosted review) that no such result exists.
